Contract:
**Port/Adapter/Service dependency graph — mandatory in `## Module Contracts`**, one level above the per-entity DbC prose: the individual Port/Adapter blocks below answer "what does each contract promise", this graph answers "who depends on whom, in which direction" — a relationship among ≥2 elements, so it is a picture, not a bullet list (`AX_INFOGRAPHIC_FIRST`, `formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`). Nodes = every Port / Adapter / Service this module defines or consumes from a sibling; edges = `implements` (Adapter → Port) and `depends on` (Service → Port), arrows drawn in the dependency direction — toward the more stable side (Stable Dependencies principle: an Adapter depends on its Port, never the reverse). Placed directly under the one-line human summary, above the folded `` block:
```markdown OrderService ──depends on──▶ PaymentGatewayPort ◀──implements── StripeAdapter ```
**Floor, never nothing:** a module with zero Ports/Adapters (Services only, no confirmed variability) still states that explicitly — `Граф не рисуется: в модуле нет Port/Adapter, только Service ` — the reader sees the DECISION (no abstraction layer here) instead of wondering whether the graph was forgotten. A single Port with a single Adapter and no other module depending on it draws the minimal two-node arrow above; it still earns the picture because direction-of-dependency is exactly the fact a reader must not have to infer from prose.
This ASCII form is shown in chat during STEP_4_CONTRACTS_DBC, at the point Port-vs-Service is decided (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`); the mermaid `flowchart` version under `## Module Contracts` is the same shape converted at write time — never a fresh diagram invented then.

**Call Chain — mandatory in `## Module Contracts`, right after `DBC_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_FORMAT`, whenever the module's inventory lists ≥2 abstractions** (entities and/or Ports/Adapters/ Services combined). The dependency graph above answers "who depends on whom"; this rung answers a distinct question — "who calls whom, IN WHAT ORDER, for the one main scenario" — a relationship among ≥2 elements over time, so it earns its own picture (`AX_INFOGRAPHIC_FIRST`, `formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`).
Two equally valid forms — pick whichever reads clearer for THIS scenario, neither is a fallback for the other:
1. **`sequenceDiagram`** — participants in call order, request/response arrows:
```markdown ```mermaid sequenceDiagram OrderService->>PaymentGatewayPort: charge(amount) PaymentGatewayPort->>StripeAdapter: charge(amount) StripeAdapter-->>PaymentGatewayPort: receipt PaymentGatewayPort-->>OrderService: receipt ``` ```
2. **Step table** — an equally valid form for a linear scenario, no diagram penalty for choosing it over the sequence form:
```markdown | Step | Participant | Action | Data | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | OrderService | charge(amount) | amount | | 2 | PaymentGatewayPort | charge(amount) | amount | | 3 | StripeAdapter | receipt | receipt | | 4 | PaymentGatewayPort | receipt | receipt | ```
Caption per `DIAGRAM_CAPTION_FORMAT` (`formats/diagram-vocabulary.xml`), naming the requirement IDs this call chain traces. Shown as ASCII (or the table, already text) in chat during STEP_4_CONTRACTS_DBC, right after the dependency graph, BEFORE that step's Approval Check (`AX_CHAT_BEFORE_SPEC`) — the mermaid version under `## Module Contracts` converts the same shape at write time. A module below the ≥2-abstraction threshold (a single Service, no Port/Adapter) states that explicitly instead of a silently missing rung — floor, never nothing, same discipline as `DBC_DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_FORMAT`. Mandatory for NEW module specs only — a module spec written before this rung existed is not retroactively broken by its absence (2026-08-20 visualization-chain decision, `specs/ai-skills/research/2026-08-20-visualization-chain.research.md`).

Conditions are plain-language statements per `AX_CONTRACTS_TEXTUAL_AGNOSTIC` — one testable statement per line, shared vocabulary, code syntax stays out (target-language code lives only in the Approved Usage Example). Optional fields marked «omit when none» are omitted, not filled with placeholders.
```markdown #### Port: `` - **Purpose:** <1 sentence> - **Consumers:** - **Supporting Artifacts:** - **Runtime Backing:** `not-implemented` | `simulation` | `real-runtime` - **Verification Levels:** subset of `contract` | `unit` | `integration` | `e2e` - **Deferred Runtime Scope:** None | - **Usage Waiver:** = 2 in production code> [-DL-N — only when a Decision Log entry actually backs the reason]
**Contract (DbC)** — one block per operation, not one shared block for the whole Port: - ``: - Pre: - Post: - On pre-violation: - ``: - Pre: <…> - Post: <…> - On pre-violation: <…>
**Invariants** (omit when none): what stays true across the entity's ENTIRE lifetime, independent of any single operation — a genuine class-level invariant, not a restatement of one operation's postcondition. ```
Preconditions / postconditions / invariants are decided by the DECISION being contracted, not by whether a Port happens to exist: when the module consciously forgoes a Port (single implementation, no confirmed variability or test seam per `AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE`), this same per-operation shape lives directly on the Service or Adapter instead — that choice is recorded in the Decision Log (`AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED`), not silently assumed.
**Usage Waiver** (`AX_USAGE_WAIVER_DISCIPLINE`, gennady yagni): a `<2` production-code usages entity is a YAGNI finding unless its contract carries this field with a real reason — an empty reason does not gate the finding. Cite an `-DL-N` only when the reason IS a Decision Log entry (a genuine, non-obvious call — not "split for readability"); when cited, it must actually have a heading in some Decision Log, or the citation does not gate the finding. The agent sets the label, never the operator; omit the field entirely when usage already clears the threshold (no placeholder text). Two forms:
- Internal entity: `- **Usage Waiver:** ` (or `-DL-N — ` when a decision backs it) - Public API for an external consumer (does NOT disable the rule — it still needs the label): `- **Usage Waiver (external: ):** ` (same `-DL-N` rule)

Same language rules as `DBC_PORT_FORMAT`: plain-language statements per `AX_CONTRACTS_TEXTUAL_AGNOSTIC`, one per line. Default: DbC conditions live on the Port — the Adapter declares implementation facts (side effects, runtime backing). Exception: when this Adapter has no Port behind it (a conscious `AX_PORTS_AND_ABSTRACTIONS_DISCIPLINE` choice, logged in the Decision Log), the Adapter carries the **Contract (DbC)** block itself, in the same per-operation shape as `DBC_PORT_FORMAT` — DbC does not disappear just because there is no Port.
```markdown #### Adapter: `` - **Implements:** `` (``) — omit when this Adapter has no Port - **Purpose:** <1 sentence> - **Supporting Artifacts:** - **Runtime Backing:** `not-implemented` | `simulation` | `real-runtime` - **Verification Levels:** subset of `contract` | `unit` | `integration` | `e2e` - **Deferred Runtime Scope:** None | - **Usage Waiver:** = 2 in production code> [-DL-N — only when a Decision Log entry actually backs the reason]
**Contract (DbC)** — ONLY when this Adapter has no Port (else the contract lives there, see `DBC_PORT_FORMAT`); same per-operation Pre / Post / On-pre-violation shape, plus Invariants when genuinely class-level: - ``: - Pre: <…> - Post: <…> - On pre-violation: <…>
**Side Effects:** - ```
Same `Usage Waiver` rule as `DBC_PORT_FORMAT` — see there for the two forms and the citation requirement.
